title.en: Color, normal and material-role parity validation

summary: Validate UV/tangent orientation, texture channel roles, transfer functions and baked-versus-runtime lighting ownership with isolated fixtures before judging a composed look.
objective: Each imported material input has the declared UV set, channel packing, transfer function, tangent orientation and lighting owner, and controlled diagnostic views expose swaps, inversions or double-lighting.
applies_when: A Blender-authored glTF uses PBR textures, tangent-space normals, multiple UV sets, baked illumination or a mix of baked and runtime light contributions.
intent_signals: check texture roles after glTF load
diagnose inverted normal or wrong UV channel
example_prompts: Validate a Blender material chart containing base color, roughness, metalness, normals and two UV sets after Three.js load.
Test a baked interior with lightmap-only, runtime-only and combined views before tone mapping.
negative_signals: one pixel threshold for every renderer
judge channel wiring from beauty render alone
bind a Combined beauty bake as a lighting-only map
not_for: Physical calibration of real materials or displays.
Proving visual identity across distinct render engines.

principles: Test transport semantics before aesthetic similarity. A convincing beauty render can hide a swapped ORM channel, incorrect color transfer, mirrored tangent basis or duplicated light contribution.

Use separate acceptance regimes: exact texture role and TEXCOORD references, numeric factor/channel probes, directional visual tests for tangent normals, and contribution-isolation views for lightmaps.
Compare pre-tone linear diagnostics for lighting ratios and transfer errors, then evaluate the intended display transform separately. Do not use display pixels as linear-light measurements.

A lightmap validation begins from a contribution manifest. The bake and runtime may share the final look only when direct, indirect, AO and emission ownership is declared without accidental duplication.
implementation: Author a compact Blender chart with labeled dielectric and metal patches, independent red/green/blue packed-channel probes, an asymmetric tangent-space normal stamp crossing a mirrored or rotated UV boundary, and two deliberately different UV grids. Freeze the exact exported mesh and texture files used by the check.

Inspect the glTF material JSON and accessors: record material factors, image/texture indices, channel roles, normal scale, and each texture's texCoord. In Three.js inspect loaded material slots and texture colorSpace annotations for the pinned revision.

Render or inspect one variable at a time when runtime evidence is authorized: unlit/base-color identification, roughness-only response, metalness boundary, four-direction normal lighting, UV index colors, lightmap-only, runtime-only and combined. Keep environment, exposure, camera and tone mapping fixed within each comparison.

For baked illumination, use a lighting-only product suitable for the runtime slot and record whether direct, indirect, AO and emissive contributions are present. Disable runtime copies for the isolation pass, then re-enable only contributions excluded by policy.
Record exact wiring failures separately from visual-regime failures. A transport pass can coexist with an appearance mismatch caused by renderer, tone mapper, environment or unsupported extension.
observable_checks: Base color and emissive inputs decode as color data while normal, roughness and metalness remain non-color data; the declared packed channels drive only their intended response.
The UV identification grid proves the referenced TEXCOORD set for every texture; tangent detail stays raised rather than dented as the light moves through four directions.
A pre-tone neutral ramp reveals no unintended transfer-function application, clipping or channel multiplication within the declared numeric tolerance.
Lightmap-only and runtime-only views account for the combined result; an overbright receiver or duplicated shadow/direct lobe fails the ownership manifest.
Intentional stylization remains valid when its altered values and contribution ownership are declared and repeatable.

creative_affordances: Use exaggerated probe colors, graphic normals or theatrical baked light to make errors legible; the test chart need not resemble the final art direction.
known_limits: A controlled chart does not certify every texture or camera in a production scene.
Tone mapping, display calibration and backend differences require their own declared regime.
Core glTF does not itself define the application lightmap binding asserted by a Three.js scene.
Authored and source-checked procedure; no bake, export, decode or render was run.

claims.statement: glTF 2.0 defines TEXCOORD-indexed texture bindings, sRGB decoding for base color, linear transfer for metallic-roughness and normal data, green roughness and blue metalness packing, and tangent-space normal semantics.
claims.scope: Normative glTF 2.0.1 core metallic-roughness material semantics; extensions and application lightmaps require separate checks.

source_refs.locator: Sections 3.7.2 attributes; 3.8 texture coordinates; 3.9.2 metallic-roughness; 3.9.3 additional textures; 5.20 and 5.30 texCoord

claims.statement: Three.js documents a Linear-sRGB working space, sRGB annotations for common color textures, no color-space annotation for common non-color maps, and separate output conversion; open-domain lightmaps may use Linear-sRGB formats such as OpenEXR.
claims.scope: Live official Three.js color-management guide read 2026-09-08; actual file encoding and renderer revision must be recorded.

source_refs.locator: Roles of color spaces: Input, Working and Output color spaces; color and non-color textures
